title: Weight Coding: Evolving Web-Scale Recommenders through Direct Weight Edits with LLM Agents
read_level: full (arXiv HTML v1, all sections 1-6; inline math dropped by text extraction; figures read from captions only)
metadata_mismatch: none (abstract contains a duplicated word 'and and' in both metadata and HTML)
why_wsp: An LLM coding agent (Opus 5.5) inspects the structure and weights of Pinterest production recommenders, forms hypotheses and applies discrete weight edits (resets, rescales, branch removal, steering, interpolation) with forward-only evaluation feedback; some values are additionally tuned by an evolution-strategy search the agent launches over selected parameters.
facets: application domain: web-scale recommender systems (retrieval, generative retrieval, ranking)
domain: industrial recommender systems (two-tower retrieval, generative retrieval, multi-task ranking)
editor: Opus 5.5 with Max thinking as LLM coding agent in a sandboxed shell; evolution strategy (antithetic Gaussian perturbations, rank-transformed scores, Adam updates) used for 'search' edits
target: Pinterest Image Search two-tower retriever (147M params; DHEN interaction module 13.6M), PinRec generative retriever (106M), Image Search ranker (1.37B, MMoE)
interface: code/tensor tools (sandboxed shell with access to production code, training platform, query engine, model artifacts; cached edit-evaluate engine rewriting TorchScript parameters in GPU memory)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (scan -> filter -> edit or ES search -> validate; multiple iterations, re-search for composition)
self_editing: no; agent edits separate recommender models (paper mentions RSI of the editing process only as a possibility)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Table 2: r4 changed 65.6k (0 searched), F04 128, L01 2,064 (2,064 searched), L07 67.7k (2,128 searched), L05 13.6M changed (2,448 searched). "Resetting a 64-dimensional layer normalization (LayerNorm) gain ... to one can change 64 values with no free parameter." (Sec 3.1)

headline_results.quote: weight coding improves held-out recall@10 of production model by up to 15.0 percentage points (+24% relative) with few edits in about 1/4 GPU hours of a full post-training finetune
Edit F04 resets the L0 gain and the L1 offset, and changing all these values gains 10.1 points under the production evaluator
Its four scalar settings yield a gain of 8.8 points.

headline_results.claim: ES search over trained mixing matrices
headline_results.quote: Searching five DHEN mixing matrices of 2,064 values, from trained weights for 150 steps gives edit L01, with a production gain of 13.7 points.
After reinitializing all 13.6M DHEN parameters, searching only its mixing matrices and LayerNorms with 2,448 values, gives edit L05. It gains 9.8 points under the production evaluator
Combining edit r4 directly with L01 lowers its four-day gain from 14.1 to 10.2 points
Unordered R@1 | +2.31 pp ... Ordered R@1 | +2.64 pp
Fresh share in the top-10 spans 2% at ... to 70% at
These edits raise saves from the source by 8.4-10.7% per user and 4.3-5.3% per impression.
headline_results.where: Sec 4.7; Table 4 (~10M users per group, ~1 week)

headline_results.quote: this rate tracks the production recall@10 gain with Pearson correlation 0.97

cost.quote: a full loop spends 8.6 GPU hours on average and it took 4 loops to find the best model reported in this work, only 24.6% of the finetune
a surface-level post-training run takes about 140 GPU hours across 8 A100
the agent evaluated over 2,000 edit configurations and about 190,000 search candidates
An end-to-end two-tower iteration takes less than 2 hours before finding a handful candidates.

baselines_and_controls: Production model (trained/fine-tuned); comparison to a typical launch ('a common launch only improves around 1%'); a retrain without weight decay on 1-D params; diagnostic embedding-collapse edit used to motivate pessimistic tie-breaking; online A/B against production. No LLM-free/random-edit control or matched-compute ES-only baseline reported.
runs_and_variance: Held-out days used; per-day results described (e.g. '+13.8 on the worst day'); ranker z-scores 7.8 to 10.5; 'The two whole-DHEN search with different seeds follow similar trajectories.' No systematic seed variance reported for agent runs.
robustness_of_edits: Tested across held-out days, separate corpus, full corpus and recall@1000 (Sec 5.1); online A/B. Survival under checkpoint refresh or distribution shift stated as open (Sec 5.3). Not tested against fine-tuning or quantization.
verification: none formal; validation protocol of dev/filter/held-out days and production evaluator comparison 'tensor by tensor' (Sec 3.5)
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a; paper notes 'allowing agent to access and analyze experiment results and source code often help' and transfer from other models 'can be negative' (Sec 4.2)
limitations_stated: Gains across dates/corpora 'doesn't rule out adaptive overfitting or biases shared across dates'; useful edits are model-specific; unclear whether edits survive checkpoint refreshes or distribution shifts; online feedback not automated in loop; cannibalization of other retrievers' impressions.
cites_or_builds_on: STOP (Zelikman et al. 2024) for RSI framing
notes_for_survey: Industrial deployment of agent-driven weight edits with online A/B results; does not cite the MIT WSP blog and uses the term 'weight coding'. Part of the largest gains come from ES search over a few thousand agent-selected values, so authorship of the numeric values is shared between the LLM agent (site selection, discrete edits) and a zeroth-order optimizer.
